title: Cheap subsampling bootstrap confidence intervals with applications to longitudinal causal inference
abstract: The bootstrap is widely used to construct confidence intervals but may perform poorly for some estimators. We consider semiparametric estimators that use cross-validation to estimate nuisance pa- rameters and can be computationally expensive in large datasets. We illustrate potential problems with bootstrapping with replacement when cross-validation is used and extend the cheap bootstrap confidence interval to subsampling without replacement for asymptotically linear estimators. We establish asymp- totically valid coverage with few bootstrap replications when the subsample size is chosen appropriately as a function of the sample size. Empirical experiments demonstrate computational advantages over resampling with replacement and explore the impact of subsample size, sample size, cross-validation and the number of bootstrap repetitions on the performance of the confidence interval. We apply the method to data from the LEADER trial to construct confidence intervals for a longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimator.
